The spot premium quotation for imported cathode is now US$80-100/t, with deals closed at US$80/t. In addition, the premium for imported SXEW cathode is quoted at US$60-70/t. Data: CRU for cathode imports is weak. This is because of the ongoing negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME as well as lower buying activity. We believe that sufficient domestic cathode supply may challenge the premium recovery. SHFE stocks rose to record highs whilst cathode imports surged in March. Furthermore, domestic cathode output remained at high levels. According to CNIA data, Chinese cathode production amounted to 366,170t in March. The figure was up by 0.4% m-o-m and 14.0% y-o-y. We believe that cathode demand will improve as a strong Q2 will provide upside support to cathode imports and spot premiums too. Otherwise, premiums might decline instead of remaining flat. © 2010 CRU International Limited **confidential** **April 2010** www.crumonitor.com # **Cathode imports surge in March** According to customs’ data, China imported 337,125t of cathode in March, up by 13.5% y-o-y and 52.9% m-o-m. arbitrage between SHFE and LME in February, and optimistic demand outlook for Q2. These factors strongly encouraged traders to import cathode. Industry sources reported that some traders increased cathode imports in February, when the arbitrage window opened. This is because they anticipated that positive arbitrage may not be sustainable for a long time, as was the case in 2009. Moreover, the volume of cathode imports contracts remained robust. However, we still believe that the volume of cathode imports in March was high. That may lead to increased domestic supply pressure in Q2 and impact demand growth. # **Chinese customs announce new rules in scrap imports** After the Chinese customs adjusted import regulations on scrap, effective 1st April 2010, another new rule was recently announced. The new requirement calls for import type categorization starting from 1st June 2010. We understand that the new rule will generate some industry development. However, it may cause negative impact to scrap impo

rters in the short term. Firstly, it may lengthen the scrap import period and cause domestic scrap supply tightness. Secondly, it means higher packaging costs that should be within an acceptable level. Thirdly, if scrap import VAT is being paid on the full content of copper, scrap prices may rise. As the discount between scrap and cathode has narrowed, consumers may increase cathode usage. As a result, this may boost cathode imports and furhter support copper prices. However, all these impacts may not come true if the Chinese customs do not implement the rule in a strict way. # **SHFE cathode stocks rise to new record highs** SHFE cathode stocks rose by 16,357t to 185,895t on 16th April. According to SHFE data, cathode inventories rose again this week but at a slower pace. SHFE cathode stocks rose to 187,907t on 23rd April, the highest level since late August 2002. This is evidence showing sufficient domestic supply and puts pressure on copper prices from rising up further. The increasing trend in SHFE stocks will not stop as the Shanghai physical market cathode discount continues to exist. SHFE inventory surges to record high

Recently, LME 3-month prices traded below US$8,000/t. Prices declined to US$7,600-7,700/t this week, partly due to Chinese announcements on real estate regulatory policies to cool the property market. Also, market sentiment was affected by the news that Goldman Sachs was involved in fraud related to a CDO product. SHFE 3-month prices declined to RMB60,070/t on 19th April. After that they hovered around RMB60,000-61,000/t. The Shanghai physical market discount remained at RMB275/t, having seen no improvement yet. We believe that copper prices may be around US$7,800/t in the next two weeks. Market insiders still have optimistic expectations for strong demand in Q2. However, high level stocks on SHFE and negative sentiment in the financial markets put pressure on copper prices. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **Susanna Keung (London):** +44 20 7903 2325 susanna.keung@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 23rd April 2010.
